# #177 — Make openbrain-memory Python package importable/installable + canonical redaction, so clients stop forking it

State: CLOSED

## Problem

The `openbrain-memory` Python package (`python/openbrain-memory/`, v0.1.0) is the intended canonical client for OB memory — transport, redaction policy, spool, session lifecycle. But it is **not currently importable/installable by downstream consumers** (no built `dist/`, not published to any index/registry the agent hosts can reach). As a result, **rtech-hermes never adopted it** and instead maintains a full FORK of the OB client (its own vendored transport + its own redaction + its own spool), which has drifted from the server contract and caused a production outage (the v5 `type:"enum"` contract bump produced invalid tool schemas → model HTTP 400 → agent hard-down).

To converge the agents onto OB's canonical client (so "agents match what OB makes"), the package must first be a real, installable dependency.

## What this issue asks (open-brain side)

Make `openbrain-memory` a properly importable/installable package so downstream repos (rtech-hermes, others) can depend on it instead of forking:

- [ ] **Build + publish path.** Produce installable artifacts (`dist/` wheel+sdist) and a documented install method the agent LXC hosts can use — e.g. `pip install git+https://github.com/rodaddy/open-brain.git#subdirectory=python/openbrain-memory`, an internal index, or a versioned wheel on the collab share. (Hosts use `uv`; confirm it resolves.)
- [ ] **Stable public API surface.** Document the importable surface (`OpenBrainClient`, redaction policy, spool, models) and a SemVer/contract-version policy so consumers can pin safely. The package already pins `CURRENT_CONTRACT_VERSION = "2026-06-19.memory-tools.v5"` — expose how consumers should track that.
- [ ] **Redaction as the single source of truth.** `policy.py` (currently ~34 patterns) is the canonical client-side redaction. The fork in rtech-hermes has DIVERGED (~40 patterns). The package's redaction must be the one true implementation that consumers import — document it as such so clients stop re-implementing it. (This is the "client redaction must be 1:1 with the server" rule; today it isn't because there are two implementations.)
- [ ] **Decide the normalizer's home.** The package has NO contract→JSON-Schema/tool normalizer today (consumers get the raw DSL). The LLM-tool-schema translation is arguably a Hermes-specific concern (depends on the consuming agent's tool-allowlist + the model's function-schema format), so it may stay client-side — BUT if multiple consumers will feed the contract to an LLM, consider a shared `contract_to_json_schema()` helper in the package so the DSL→JSON-Schema translation lives next to the contract definition (where the v5 enum/typeless shapes are known) and can't drift. At minimum, document the contract DSL (type:"enum"+values, min/max, custom semantic types like git_sha, fields-with-no-type for bare object literals, array items as type-ref strings) so client normalizers are correct. See the outage details: the contract intentionally emits a non-JSON-Schema DSL, and that's fine — but it must be documented so clients normalize correctly.

## Why now
rtech-hermes wants to retire its vendored fork and consume this package (tracked in the rtech-hermes companion issue). That migration is blocked until the package is installable + its redaction is the documented canonical source.

## Non-goal
Do NOT change the contract DSL emitted by `get_contract` to be JSON-Schema-valid — it's a deliberate internal format. The fix is making the package consumable + documented, not changing the wire format.

> ## Critical self-review
>
> - Highest-risk behavior: heuristic redaction could over-match benign identifiers or leak if downstream keeps using forked regex lists.
> - Assumptions that could be wrong: downstream consumers will import from the package root and validate the live `get_contract()` manifest instead of treating package install alone as readiness.
> - Missing/weak tests: no live canary was run; package tests use fake transports and the wheel smoke is local-only.
> - Security/permission risk: heuristic patterns are intentionally kept out of `SECRET_PATTERNS` so they do not widen fail-closed payload rejection in `agent._reject_secret_payload`.
> - Migration/deploy risk: version `0.1.1` must be pinned by downstream hosts; moving branches remain unsafe for production host installs.
> - Downstream client/runtime risk: Hermes still needs its own adapter migration and canary before retiring its vendored fork.
> - Rollback/cleanup concern: generated `dist/` artifacts are ignored and were not committed; downstream can pin the previous package version/commit if this artifact regresses.
> - Fixes made before PR: tightened the high-entropy symbol lookahead to only inspect the token body, added anti-regression tests for benign SHA-like IDs, package metadata/version behavior, source-tree package imports, and reran validation/build/smoke.
> - Known residual risk: first live downstream adoption still needs a real host canary; heuristic redaction intentionally prioritizes diagnostic readability over fail-closed write rejection for unlabeled ambiguous shapes.
